title: 1998 HMMT February Algebra Problem 9
statement: Suppose \(f(x)\) is a rational function such that \(3 f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+\frac{2 f(x)}{x}=x^{2}\) for \(x \neq 0\). Find \(f(-2)\).

solutions.text:
Let \(x=\frac{-1}{2}\). Then

\[\begin{aligned}
& 3 f(-2)+\frac{2 f\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)}{\frac{-1}{2}}=\frac{1}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow 3 f(-2)-4 f\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)= \frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}\]

Let \(x=-2\). Then

\[\begin{aligned}
& 3 f\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)+\frac{2 f(-2)}{-2}=4 \\
\Rightarrow 3 f\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)-f(-2) & =4
\end{aligned}\]

Solving this system of equations \(\{(1),(2)\}\) for \(f(-2)\) yields \(f(-2)=\frac{67}{20}\).
